what_its_for: Tiotropium is used to help you breathe easier if you have a long-term lung condition such as COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), which includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It works by relaxing and opening up the airways in your lungs so air can flow more freely. It also helps reduce sudden flare-ups of COPD symptoms. The Respimat form may also be used for asthma in adults and some children.
how_to_take: Tiotropium comes in two forms: the HandiHaler (a dry powder capsule inhaler) and the Respimat (a soft mist inhaler). For the HandiHaler: Open the device, place one capsule in the chamber, close it, press the button once to pierce the capsule, then breathe in slowly and deeply through your mouth. Hold your breath for about 10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Never swallow the capsules — they are only meant to be inhaled. For the Respimat: Prime the inhaler before first use by pressing the dose-release button 3 times (or until a mist appears). Breathe out gently, put the mouthpiece in your mouth, and breathe in slowly while pressing the button. Hold your breath for about 10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Always rinse your mouth with water after use to help prevent dryness. Use your inhaler at the same time each day for best results.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is ONE inhalation (HandiHaler: 18 mcg capsule) or TWO puffs (Respimat: 2.5 mcg per puff, total 5 mcg) taken ONCE daily. For asthma with the Respimat, the dose may be different — follow your doctor's exact instructions. Do not use more than your prescribed dose in one day. Tiotropium is a long-term, maintenance medicine — not a quick-relief rescue inhaler for sudden breathing problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule the next day. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the HandiHaler capsules in their original blister packaging and only remove a capsule right before you are ready to use it. Keep out of direct sunlight and moisture. Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). For the Respimat inhaler, store at room temperature and avoid freezing. Keep the cap closed when not in use. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the capsules or inhaler past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not use tiotropium as a rescue inhaler during a sudden asthma attack or severe breathing emergency — always keep a separate fast-acting rescue inhaler (such as albuterol) on hand for those situations. Avoid getting the medication in your eyes, as it can cause blurry vision or eye pain and may worsen glaucoma. Tell your doctor before using tiotropium if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, difficulty urinating, or kidney problems. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice in large amounts unless your doctor says it is okay. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, especially other anticholinergic drugs, since combining them can increase side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: sudden worsening of breathing or wheezing, chest pain or tightness, eye pain, redness, or blurred vision (possible sign of glaucoma), difficulty urinating or no urine output, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction), fast or irregular heartbeat, or if your regular rescue inhaler stops working as well as usual. Contact your doctor if you notice a rash, itching, or any unusual side effects. Common mild side effects like dry mouth, constipation, or a mild sore throat do not usually require emergency care but should be mentioned at your next appointment.
when_it_works: Tiotropium starts working within 30 minutes of your first dose, but it may take several days to weeks of daily use before you notice the full benefit on your breathing. It is not a cure for COPD or asthma, but with regular daily use it helps keep your airways open, reduces shortness of breath, and lowers the chance of flare-ups. Do not stop using it even if you feel better — continue taking it every day as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Tiotropium can be used in older adults, but you may be more sensitive to side effects such as dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, or difficulty urinating. Report any of these symptoms to your doctor. Kidney problems: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely if you have moderate to severe kidney disease, as the drug can build up in your body. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: There is limited information on the safety of tiotropium during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using it if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: The Respimat form may be prescribed for children 6 years and older for asthma — follow the doctor's specific dosing instructions carefully. The HandiHaler is generally only approved for adults.
